Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verses 1–3:

Surah al-Anbiya' (Makkiyyah)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿The reckoning of mankind has drawn near for them, while they are heedless and turn away.﴾ (21:1–9)

This is an extremely forceful opening. It shakes any heedless person to the core: the reckoning is at hand, yet people sit in neglect and carelessness. The Messenger presents the signs of Allah to them with great eagerness, and they turn their faces away and head in the other direction. There is an urgent need to be alert, but these people do not even have awareness of the danger. Rather, whenever a fresh attempt is made to warn them, they mock, and, considering the call unimportant, they busy themselves with play.

﴿Their hearts are heedless﴾ (21:3). Their minds, their perceptions, and the strings of their conscience and intuition are completely silent. There is no melody within them. This is a portrait of persons who are extremely careless and devoid of seriousness: they remain unserious even in the most dangerous situations, they chatter even at a place where one must be most cautious, and they defile even the most sacred stance and the most sacred place. This Qur'an, which is being presented to them, is a message from the Lord of Majesty, yet they are negligent of it. There is no dignity and no purity in them. People in whom seriousness, dignity, purity and vigour are not seen eventually become so light, dry and broken that they are no longer fit for any lofty mission, for the performance of great duties, or for bearing heavy burdens. Their lives are loose, their morals fallen, and their values cheap. Among such people a kind of shamelessness arises, and they regard even the most sacred value as trivial. They are like unbridled camels, not bound by any constitution or code, and they lose all awareness of good and evil.

People of this kind did not take this Qur'an seriously, although it was the constitution of life, the system of living, the system of action and the system of dealings. It should have been viewed with seriousness, but these people took it with extreme carelessness, like an unbridled, reckless person, and began to mock. Such people exist in every age. When the human spirit bids farewell to that purity and that sanctity of principles, society produces sick people, unbridled people, careless people, who have no aim and take nothing seriously.

This is why the believers received this surah with such seriousness and such importance that their hearts became indifferent to the world and all that is in it. In the Tarjama of Amidi, there is the account of 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah: a man of Arabia came to him, showed him great honour and esteem, and made him comfortable. After this, that man came to 'Amir again, by which time land had been allotted to him. He said: "I have obtained from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a whole valley of the land of Arabia as a grant, and I wish to give you a portion of it so that it may benefit you and your descendants after you." 'Amir said: "I have no interest any more in your grant. Today a surah has been revealed which has shaken us to the core. Now we have no further interest in the world."

﴿The reckoning of mankind has drawn near, while they are heedless and turn away﴾ (21:1).

This is the difference in hearts. On one side are living hearts that accept and are moved; on the other are dead, extinguished hearts, hearts in which every window to the entry of thought and understanding is shut. Upon these dead hearts lie the shrouds of play and amusement, and they have been buried in the graveyard of unbridled carelessness. The Qur'an has no effect upon them, because their hearts have been extinguished and they have become such that no spark of life remains within them.

﴿And the wrongdoers confide secretly to one another﴾ (21:3). The people of Makkah constantly whispered together about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his movement. These whisperings would then take the form of plots, and they would comment thus:

﴿Is this not but a human being like yourselves? Will you then submit to magic while you see?﴾ (21:3)

Indeed, these people had in reality died, and no spark of life remained in their bodies. Therefore they were not themselves affected by the Qur'an. But they would lead astray other people upon whom the Qur'an had an effect, saying: "Look, Muhammad is merely a human being like us, so why do you believe in him? Whatever effect this speech has upon you is magic. You are seeing and understanding, yet you accept the effect of this magic."

When they resorted to such worthless weapons, the Messenger of Allah was commanded to leave himself and them to the care of Allah. Whatever plots they are hatching and whatever excuses and propaganda they make to ward off the effect of the Qur'an will have no effect.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 4:

﴿قُلْ رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ الْقَوْلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ (21:4) "The Messenger said: My Lord knows every word spoken in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

Wherever in the land a whisper is made against the Islamic movement, Allah hears and knows it, for Allah is the One who knows all the sayings uttered in the heavens and the earth, and they are recorded with Him. And whatever plots they hatch, Allah informs His Messenger beforehand, for He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

They thought deeply about how to stop the effect of the Qur'an through what propaganda. They concluded that it is sorcery, a confused mixture of thoughts and scattered ideas which Muhammad gathers and presents, sometimes saying it is poetry, sometimes soothsaying.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 5:

"Nay, they say: [these are] confused dreams; nay, he has invented it; nay, he is a poet" (21:5). They keep saying "nay" after "nay." They cannot hold to any one position; they have no single opinion. The truth is that these people adopt various stratagems to find a way to stop the stirring effects of the Qur'an, which are affecting people, and they keep making claim upon claim, bringing one reason after another. Yet they remain deeply perplexed and cannot settle on any one matter. So, leaving aside all their maneuvers and statements, they come round to the view that some sign should be shown to them, like the miracles that earlier messengers had shown.

"So let them bring us a sign, as the earlier ones were sent [with signs]" (21:5). Indeed, earlier messengers had shown miracles that broke the normal course of nature. But did all those to whom the miracles were presented believe? No, they did not believe, and that is precisely why they were destroyed. This is the Divine way (sunnat Ilahiyah), and it is an unchanging law of God: when an extraordinary miracle is presented and people still do not believe, their destruction becomes inevitable.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 6:

"Not one town which We destroyed before them believed. Will they then believe?" (21:6)

This means that when a people reaches such a degree of enmity and obstinacy that it does not believe even after a tangible, extraordinary miracle, then its destruction becomes inevitable.

Miracles came again and again, nations denied them again and again, and those deniers were destroyed in history again and again. So if these people were shown a miracle of the same kind and they too did not believe, then what other outcome could there be but destruction?

﴿Will they then believe?﴾ (21:6)

Wa ma arsalna... wa ma kanu khalidin (21:7–8)

"We sent none before you but men to whom We revealed. Ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know. Nor did We give those messengers bodies that did not eat food, nor were they immortal."

It was the wisdom of Allah that messengers should be human beings, who receive revelation from Allah and convey it to the people. Every messenger who passed before had a body and a soul, and having a body and a soul, they also ate food, because eating is a necessary requirement of the body. And in terms of humanity and physicality, they were not beings of eternal life either. If you do not know this, then learn about the physicality of the messengers and about eating and drinking from the People of the Book, because the People of the Book had more knowledge of the sciences of the prophets than the Arabs did.

The truth is that all the messengers were human beings. They lived as humans live, so that their practical lives would take the form of Shariah. Their practical conduct would be a model of high life for people, because a call that is alive and that has a model and example in the practical form of life is the one that is effective. People see that this call is established in practical, embodied form and has been given a practical shape.

If messengers were not human, they would not eat and drink, would not walk in markets, would have no social life with women, and their hearts would have no human feelings and inclinations; then a deep relationship between them and other people could not be established. They would be unable to understand the inclinations that humans have, and humans would not understand them well, nor follow them, because in their lives there would be no model for humans to follow.

If a caller does not understand the inclinations of the people he calls, does not understand their consciousness, emotions and desires, and does not enter among the people but keeps himself far from them, does not walk with the people and the people do not walk with him, then however much he shouts and makes speeches before the people, they will by no means be influenced by his speeches, because between them lie the distances of feeling and consciousness.

Every caller whose deed does not confirm his words, his words will strike the ears of people and return. They will not penetrate the hearts, even if his words are forceful and his speech eloquent. The simple statement that is backed by action, by which the speaker himself is affected, that alone can be beneficial and can create movement in people.

Those who proposed that the messenger should be an angel, just as some people today declare the messenger to be devoid of human qualities, are unaware of the reality that angels, by their creative make-up and their nature, cannot live a life like humans, because they are not capable, according to body and its requirements, of understanding the consciousness of humans. Therefore, in this respect, it is simply not possible for them to live a life like humans. A messenger must understand these human feelings and requirements, and must also act upon these feelings and requirements in his practical life, so that he can become a practical code of life for the people.

These matters are in their place, but the greatest point is that if the messenger were an angel, the great honour that Allah bestowed upon the human species in this surah would have been denied to humankind. It would not have been that one human from among humans establishes contact with the higher world or converses with Allah.

In any case, it is the sunnah of Allah in the choice of messengers that the messenger be a human, and it is also His sunnah that He saves them and destroys the extravagant and the deniers.

Thumma sadaqnahumul wa'd... al-musrifin (21:9)

"Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whomever We willed, and We destroyed the extravagant."

Just as there is a sunnah for the choice of messengers, so too there is this sunnah for the deniers: Allah destroyed them and, along with them, those who truly believed, but whose deeds did not confirm their belief. Allah destroys those who transgress limits.

The polytheists, who harassed the Messenger ﷺ and his Muslim companions and went beyond all bounds in denying them, were warned by Allah with this sunnah, and it was made clear to them that it is a great mercy of Allah upon them that He did not send a material, extraordinary miracle which, had they denied it as the earlier peoples had denied, would have led to their destruction as well. Instead of that extraordinary miracle, Allah has given you the miracle of the Qur'an, and this Book is a source of honour and dignity for you, because it is in your language; it sets your lives in order, and it shapes your upbringing and training in such a way that it makes you a community worthy of mention. This Book lies open before the people; they should reflect upon it and, through it, keep climbing the ladder of human advancement.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 10:

﴿Indeed We have sent down to you a Book in which is your mention. Then will you not reason?﴾ ( ” ۔

The Qur'an is a miracle that is an open miracle for all generations. It is not a miracle whose manifestation is confined to one generation, after which people are impressed by it and it comes to an end. It is a lasting and enduring miracle.

Through the Qur'an, the Arabs also gained great fame, when they carried its message to the East and the West. Before this, they were not a people of any note, nor did they have anything worthy of mention to give to humanity. As long as the Arabs held firmly to this Book, they guided all of humanity through it, and they too were successful, and because of it, all of humanity also attained success and prosperity. When the Arabs abandoned this Book, humanity also abandoned them, and the mention of the Arabs began to disappear among people. They became a hanger-on to the caravan of humanity, and anyone among humans may snatch them up as he wishes. But while they held this Book firmly, people were snatched up in their environment, and they remained safe.

The truth is, what can the Arabs give to humanity other than the Qur'an? What else do they have besides the Qur'an? They have no thought to present before humanity other than Qur'anic thought. If they present this Book before humanity, humanity will recognise them; it will mention them and raise them on its heads, because it will receive a beneficial message from the Arabs. But if they present the Arabs merely as a nation before humanity, they should know what their status is and what they are. What is the worth of this lineage apart from this Book? Humanity recognised the Arabs through this Book, through the Islamic worldview and through the system of life derived from this Book. The position they attained in humanity was not because they were Arabs, for being Arab alone is nothing in the history of humanity, and the word "Arab" has no place in the dictionary of civilisation. The Arabs were, and are, recognised through Islamic civilisation and culture. Islamic civilisation, Islamic thought, Islamic philosophy and Islamic culture will be found by name in the dictionary of culture, but the word Arab has no name in it.

The Qur'an here points to this very reality. The polytheists are addressed and told that this Book is your identity. But you received the new teachings in this Book with heedlessness, aversion, denial and mockery.

﴿Indeed We have sent down to you a Book in which is your mention. Then will you not reason?﴾ (12 : 01) "O people, We have sent to you a Book in which is your mention. Do you not understand?"

It was a mercy of Allah upon the Arab polytheists that no miracle that breaks habitual patterns (khariq 'adat) was presented to them through the Prophet (ﷺ), otherwise they would have rejected it, and their destruction would have followed in the same way as the divine way (sunnat Ilahiyyah) that occurred to many nations and many towns in history. Here, Allah shows, in the form of a vivid scene, the annihilation and the ruin and destruction of such nations.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 11:

وکم قصمنا من قریۃ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ حصیدا خمدین (11 تا 51) ”

The word qasam means to cut off with force. The very sound of this word also reveals its meaning. From its pronunciation it becomes clear that the wrongdoing towns were broken and smashed with great force and severity, so completely that their very existence was ended, and their condition became such that they were reduced to dust.

وانشانا ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ اخرین (12 : 11) "And We raised up after them another people." Here the verb qasam falls upon the towns, and both the towns and their inhabitants are ground to pieces, whereas the verb insha' (raising up) falls only upon a people: first a people comes into being, and then it establishes towns. This is the reality of the event: destruction descends upon towns, and the population also perishes in it. And when something is raised up, the peoples are raised first, and then they settle and build towns. But the manner in which the destruction and ruin are presented in the form of a scene is the distinctive artistic style of the Holy Qur'an.

When this destruction comes, the scene of the people in it is also very strange. Their condition is like that of mice trapped in a cage: until they are destroyed, they keep running about inside the cage.

When they sensed Our punishment, behold, they began to flee from it.

That is, they began to run away from the village in every direction. They realised that the punishment of God had come, as though this frantic running would save them from the punishment of God. As though they could run so fast that the punishment of God would be left behind them. But their scrambling is exactly like that of a mouse running about in a cage: it runs without thought and without any awareness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verses 13–14:

Do not run away; return to your comfortable homes and the luxuries in which you were enjoying yourselves, so that perhaps you may be questioned. (21:13, cited as 12:31 in the source text, corrected to the verse in question)

This is your town; do not flee from it. Within it is all your equipment and within it are your dwellings in which you indulged in luxury. Return, perhaps you will be asked how you spent this wealth. What answer will they give to that question? That was a serious joke with them.

Now, when they grow tired, they understand that the punishment of God has encircled them and that this stampede can no longer benefit them. This running cannot take them outside the circle of punishment, so they change: they acknowledge their crime and seek repentance and forgiveness.

They said: "Woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers." (21:14, cited as 12:41 in the source text, corrected to the verse in question) But what can be done now? The time of respite has already ended. Now they may keep saying whatever they wish. Even if these people keep confessing their guilt and repenting until death, it will be of no benefit.

"فما زالت ... خمدين" (12:51): "They continued to cry out until We made them like a harvested field, extinguished, with not a spark of life left in them."

This was a field of human beings in which there was neither movement nor warmth. Until then, that town had been one in which life could be seen running everywhere, and this village was extremely beautiful.

Here the Qur'an now establishes a connection between the outlook on life that was being discussed and the divine cosmic law (sunnah takwiniyyah) of Allah according to which this universe operates. It is this cosmic law that cut down their harvest and crushed it, because they did not follow the legislative law (sunnah tashri'iyyah) of the Lord, the Exalted. Therefore it becomes established that the truth upon which this universe stands and the truth upon which the call of the prophets stands are one, and that the universe, the heavens and the earth are connected to these two realities.

When the new guidance of the Islamic call came to the polytheists, they received it with mockery and ridicule, and turned away absorbed in frivolity. They remained heedless of how important and true this call was, that the Day of Reckoning is near, and they are heedless of that too. Rather, when they mock, the cosmic law of Allah also continues to do its work, and it too takes notice of the denial and aversion of the polytheists, because truth is one, whether it is in the law (shari'ah) or in the universe.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 21, verse 16–17:

﴿وما خلقنا السماء...﴾ ... ﴿مما تصفون﴾ (21:16–17) ”

Allah, Exalted is He, created this universe according to a wisdom and a plan; it has a purpose. This universe was not created as mere sport or play. It is a wise act, not a merely accidental process. With the same seriousness, truth and purposefulness with which the heavens and the earth were created, Messengers were also sent, Books were revealed, duties of office were determined, and Shari'ah (divine law) and legal systems were established. Therefore, purposefulness and seriousness are the foundation of this universe. Its functioning also has a purpose. There is a purpose in giving human beings a worldview, and there is purposefulness and seriousness in the reckoning and accounting after death.

If Allah had wanted to make a plaything, He would have made it in His own presence. It would have been a purely personal play, and it would have had no connection with the other creatures of Allah. This is merely an argumentative and dialectical supposition: "If We had wished to take a plaything, and that alone was what We had to do, We would have taken it from Our own presence." Just as the grammarians say that this is only imtina' li-imtina' (impossibility for the sake of impossibility) — that is, after "law" (if) there is a conditional clause and a second clause which is the answer of the condition. The meaning is that the occurrence of both these clauses is impossible and inconceivable. Since Allah has not intended it, play has not occurred at all. Neither did any play occur with Allah, nor did it occur in any matter outside. And this play is not possible, because the intention of Allah has not turned towards it.

In ﴿in kunna fa'ilin﴾ (12:71), the meaning is ma kunna fa'ilin, that is: "We were never going to do such a thing; We were never people who would do it." So this is a supposition for the sake of debate, and through it the fact is established that all matters related to the Divine Being are, like the Being of Allah, eternal, everlasting, and not perishable. If Allah had intended play, this play would not have been a new matter; it would also have been eternal like the Divine Being, everlasting and perpetual, because it would have been connected with the Eternal and Everlasting Being. For this reason the word ﴿min ladunna﴾ ("from Our own presence") was used. But Allah's established law is that no matter should be done as play; rather, every matter should be done with seriousness and truth, and it should be the truth. Thus truth prevails over falsehood.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 21, verse 18:

﴿Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes its head, and behold, it vanishes.﴾ (21:18) ["Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes its head, and it vanishes away." – the Urdu rendering here uses ﴿بل﴾ and the verse's wording ﴿زاھق﴾ (12:81 as cited in the source)]

In grammar, the word ﴿بل﴾ (bal, "but rather") is used for idrab (a turning away from one statement to another), meaning that the speaker sets aside one matter and takes up another. Here, setting aside the matter of play and amusement, it is stated that the real reality is that there is a struggle between truth and falsehood, and the Divine way (sunnat Ilahiyyah) is that in this struggle truth is granted victory.

The manner of expression in this scene is extremely concrete, perceptible, full of life and full of motion. The picture is that truth is a projectile in the hand of divine power; Power throws it, it strikes the head of falsehood and smashes its skull, and falsehood is wiped off the face of existence in an instant.

This is a settled sunnah, and truth is fundamental within this universe. Truth has a deep role in the existence of the universe. Falsehood is, as it were, outside the boundary of the universe. If it appears somewhere, that is temporary; its strength cannot be deep, and Allah keeps driving falsehood away. Through truth, Allah Himself keeps bombarding falsehood and keeps breaking its head. Therefore, that upon which Allah's bombardment falls, that which the hand of power destroys, has no permanence. Never, never!

Some superficial people think that at this time the practical situation on this earth is against what Allah, the All-Knowing, All-Aware, is saying. Apparently the circumstances are the opposite. This question arises in those historical intervals in which falsehood sometimes appears swollen. It seems as though its rule will continue. And in those intervals, truth and the people of truth are so downtrodden, dejected and dust-covered that they appear defeated. The reality is that in human history such things keep happening during brief intervals. Allah sometimes lengthens these intervals a little, but this is for the trial of the people of truth. After that, the unseen hand of the Divine sunnah begins the bombardment. This is the Divine sunnah, and upon this sunnah the system of the heavens and earth stands, and upon it also stands the system of Islamic missions.

For those whose faith is firm, not even a slight doubt can arise in their hearts that the foundation of this universe is truth. They cannot doubt that Allah, supporting the callers to truth, hurls a projectile at falsehood and knocks its brain out. If Allah tests the people of truth for some time, they should understand that this is their trial. They should remain steadfast on the path of truth and come up to the standard of this trial. They should understand that there are weaknesses within them, and Allah wants these to be removed, and that they should be prepared for the victory of this truth. They should do the work of the hand of power: remove their weaknesses, and develop perfection within themselves. The more quickly they complete their preparations, the more quickly the period of their trial will end, and then whatever projectile Allah hurls at falsehood will be through their hands. It will be the scene of ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ (8:17), and suddenly falsehood will be annihilated from this world. Remember that the end of falsehood is decreed.

﴿Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes its head, and behold, it vanishes.﴾ And Allah does what He wills.

(In Russia, the hand of divine power has accomplished this work. Translator.)

The Qur'an is impressing upon the polytheists of Makkah this reality, those who used to say such things about the Qur'an as: it is magic, it is poetry, it is fabrication. Yet it is true, and the Qur'an is attacking falsehood, breaking its head, and soon falsehood and shirk will be wiped out (from the Arabian Peninsula). They are warned that the things you fabricate about the Qur'an or the Islamic movement are a means of your destruction. (﴿And woe to you for what you describe﴾, 21:18.) After this, in contrast to their disobedience and aversion, an example of the obedience of creatures who submit is presented before them. This example is drawn from the lives of those who, compared to them, are closer to Allah Most High, yet despite this closeness they are engaged in His worship night and day, and they do not even tire of worship.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verses 19–20:

﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth...﴾ ... ﴿...they go astray.﴾

No one knows the complete knowledge of what is in the heavens and the earth except Allah. It is Allah alone who can encompass everything. Only He knows with certainty about human beings. Believers also affirm the existence of jinn and angels, because the Qur'an mentions them, yet about these two creations too we know only as much as the Creator has given us knowledge of. It is possible that there are other intelligent creatures on other celestial bodies besides these two, and that their form and appearance correspond to the environment and natural conditions of those planets, but this knowledge too is with Allah alone.

﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ (12:91) — "Whatever creation exists in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah." So we affirm every creation of which we have knowledge, and whatever we do not know, we leave to the Creator of the universe.

﴿And those who are with Him﴾ — The closest meaning of this is that the intended ones are the angels, but why should we restrict its meaning? It includes the angels and other creations. Its "with Him" or "ʿindahu" meaning does not express spatial location in relation to Allah, but rather indicates nearness.

﴿And those who are with Him... and they do not tire﴾ (12:91) — "Those who are with Allah neither consider themselves too great to worship Him, nor do they grow weary." Just as the polytheists of Makkah turn away from the servitude of Allah out of mere arrogance, these beings do not tire; that is, day and night they continually worship Allah, glorify Him, and declare His oneness.

As for human beings, their entire life can become worship, and they can keep themselves in a state of continuous worship like the angels, if they serve and obey Allah throughout their whole life, even though some of their actions are of a personal nature, such as eating and drinking.

That is, the countless and varied creations of Allah, whatever is in the heavens and the earth, are busy worshipping Allah day and night; but the polytheists turn away from the worship of Allah alone and worship and call upon other gods. Their conduct is very evil. Yet the system of night and day and the natural law operating throughout this whole universe are clear evidence that the Governor of the universe is Allah, alone without partner. Moreover, if they seek transmitted proof, the Qur'an and all the heavenly scriptures agree that Allah is the one God, and this is the call of all the messengers and books.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verses 21–22:

"Or have they taken gods from the earth who can raise the dead? ... Say: 'Bring your proof. This is the Reminder for those with me and the Reminder for those before me.' But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away. We did not send any messenger before you except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me." (21:21–25)

Is it that they have taken other gods besides Him? Say to them, "Bring your proof. This Book is here, which contains a reminder for those with me, and these are the Books that contained a reminder for those before me." But most of them are unaware of the truth, and so they turn away. We did not send any messenger before you except that We revealed to him: there is no god but Me, so worship Me.

Asking about these people, whether they have taken gods besides Allah, is a rhetorical question of denial. Then describing these gods as having the attribute that they cause people to die and then bring them back to life is a mockery of their gods, because the true concept of a god is precisely that he resurrects people after death and calls them to account. It is asked in mockery: tell us, do these gods of theirs keep busy with the work of gathering and scattering (the dead)? If not, and the polytheists themselves admit that they do not, then why do they regard them as gods, when they do not even possess the primary attribute of divinity?

This is practical argumentation and practical logic. Now observe another realistic, practical argument:

"Had there been in them gods other than Allah, both would have been corrupted" (21:22). That is, if there were other gods besides One Allah in the heavens and the earth, the system of both would have been disrupted. This universe stands upon a law of nature that establishes a complete connection among all its parts, and all its parts are interconnected. The movement of each single part is linked with the movement of the whole universe. This single law depends upon the command and will of a single lawgiver. If the governing beings of the universe were many, their wills would also be many, and their laws would also be many. The manifestation of the will of one being would differ from the manifestation of the will of the being that enforces a law and ordinance. Had this been so, this complete system of the universe would have long since collided with itself, lost its harmony, and there would have been great upheavals in the universe every day. This connection, order and harmony within the universe is so evident and observable that not even the most committed atheist can deny it. Those whose nature is sound understand that a single law operates throughout this entire universe, and this uniformity is a significant testimony that a single system operates throughout the whole universe, and it has one Creator and Governor, so there is no corruption in its structure or its course.

"Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe" (21:22). That is, Allah, Lord of the Throne, is exalted above what these people fabricate. They claim that Allah has associates, while He is far above what they say. He is the Lord of the Throne. The Throne is a symbol and indication of Allah's sovereign authority, His dominion and encompassing power, and His exaltedness. Allah is pure of what they have fabricated, and the soundness, order, harmony and uniformity of this very universe bears witness against what they say.

﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ (21:23). ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, and they are questioned.﴾ He is fully dominant over His servants. His will is free. There is no restriction or bond upon Him, and no other will can stand in its way. Even the law of destiny (qadr) which He Himself has established cannot become an obstacle before His will. Questioning and accountability take place according to a standard, a measure and limits that have been laid down. Some people are so gripped by thought that they keep asking strange and foolish questions: Why did Allah do this? Why did He create this thing? What is its wisdom? Their intention is that they cannot understand this wisdom. Such people also adopt a very irreverent attitude towards the Creator of the universe in this matter, just as they go beyond the limits of human understanding, because the limited faculties of perception of a human being cannot discover the cause and reason of everything.

Allah is the Being who has knowledge of everything. The governance of every thing in the whole universe is in His hand. He encompasses all things. He is the Absolute Powerful, the Governor, the Ruler and the Wise.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 25:

"We did not send any Messenger before you except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me alone" (21:25). Ever since Allah sent Messengers to guide people, the foundational principle of their call and teaching has been the belief in Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah). This has never changed to this day. That is, the Ilah (object of worship) and the Rabb (Lord) are one and the same. He alone is the Lord, and there can be no separation between Uluhiyyah (divinity) and Rububiyyah (lordship); whoever is the Ilah is also the Rabb. Therefore, in these teachings there is no shirk in Uluhiyyah, sovereignty, or worship, and this belief is as firmly established as the order of this universe is firm. **Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, *Fi Zilal al-Quran* (Urdu translation), on Surah 21, verses 30–31:**

﴿Have not those who disbelieved considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We separated them… each in an orbit they swim.﴾

This is a tour of the universe that is visible to us, while the hearts and minds of people are completely heedless of the proofs and evidences present in it. If it is contemplated with an open heart and mind, there are in it signs that seize hold of reason and wisdom. Only a seeing eye is needed.

That the heavens and the earth were once joined together and that We later separated them is worthy of reflection. In the field of astronomy, as human knowledge advances, it confirms this statement of the Qur'an, which the Qur'an made fourteen hundred years ago. The conclusion of the theories human beings have formulated to date is that the galaxy of the sun, in which there are the sun, the moon, the earth and the other planets that follow them, was first a "sadim" (nebula), and later these bodies separated and took their present form. And that the earth was a part of the sun itself, from which it separated and cooled down.

But this is only one of the astronomical theories. Today it stands, tomorrow it will be blown away, and another, more firm theory will take its place. It is not the method of Muslims to impose an uncertain theory of astronomers upon a certain verse and then interpret it accordingly. Today we accept it and tomorrow we reject it. Therefore, in this interpretation of the Holy Qur'an, we have not adopted the method of reconciling the Qur'an with modern scientific theories. But scientific theories are one thing, and scientific facts are another. Scientific facts are those that are proven by experiment, for example: it is a scientific fact that matter expands with heat, water turns into vapour when heated, and water freezes from cold. Other such experiments are in fact scientific facts. These scientific facts are different from scientific and astronomical theories.

The Holy Qur'an is not a book of scientific theories. Nor was the Qur'an revealed so that experiments be conducted on it as in science. In fact, the Qur'an is a complete system of life. Moreover, Islam also sets limits for reason so that it works within its limits. Islam also lays down a code for society so that it gives reason freedom to function. But Islam does not interfere in scientific details, nor does it go into particulars. By correcting the direction of reason, Islam leaves these matters to reason.

The Qur'an occasionally points to cosmic facts, for example ﴿Have those who disbelieved not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, and We separated them?﴾ (12:03) ﴿The heavens and the earth were joined together, then We parted them﴾. We believe in this reality solely because it is mentioned in the Qur'an, although we do not know the details of how it happened: how the earth separated from the heavens, or how the heavens separated from the earth. We accept those scientific theories also to the extent that they are not contrary to the reality mentioned in the Qur'an. But we do not do this: place astronomical theories before us and run the verses of the Qur'an behind them, and take the certificate of the Qur'an's truthfulness from those theories, because the certain reality is the Qur'an. At most we can say that today's astronomical theories are not contrary to the general content of this verse, which was stated in this verse centuries ago.

Now we come to the second part of this verse, in which it is said: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ (12:03). This verse also points to a most important reality. Scientists regard its discovery and proof as a great achievement, and they praise Darwin, who discovered that water is the basic cradle of life, and proved this reality through experiment.

There is no doubt that when scientists reached this reality, it was a very great discovery. But what has come in the Holy Qur'an is not a new discovery for us, and the discovery and experiment of scientists does not add to a Muslim's faith in the Qur'an. The basis of our belief in the Qur'an is that it is from Allah, and we believe in it. It is not the basis that modern scientific theories prove the facts given in the Holy Qur'an. Yes, we can say that Darwin's theory of evolution and development is correct and proven reality to the extent that it considers water necessary for life.

Fourteen hundred years ago, the Holy Qur'an had already directed the disbelievers to this: just reflect on this universe, look at its wonders. The Qur'an severely criticised them for not observing the universe, and said: ﴿Will they then not believe?﴾ (12:03) Whereas the universe spread around them is calling out: believe in Allah.

And here are further cosmic scenes: ﴿And We placed firm mountains on the earth lest it shake with them﴾. What is established here is that on the earth We placed great mountains so that it would not tilt to one side with human beings on it and so that there would be no instability within it. Balance is created in different ways. For example, sometimes the internal pressure that is inside the earth creates balance, and sometimes external pressure creates balance, and this pressure differs in different regions. Sometimes it happens that mountains are high in one place while in another place balance is achieved through deep depressions in the earth. Whatever the case, this verse proves in general that the balance of the earth is connected with the mountains. Therefore we invite rational sciences and experiments: the Qur'an has announced a reality as a reality; you establish it through scientific experiments. And this is the real field of human reason and of working on scientific subjects. We should have intuitive certainty in this proclamation of the Holy Qur'an, and should undertake further research in this universe to prove it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 21, verse 33:

﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي...﴾ to ﴿يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ (21:33): "It is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each one is floating in its own orbit."

Night and day are the two great colours of this universe, and the sun and the moon are two great celestial bodies. Both have a deep connection with human life on this earth, indeed with the very essence of life. Moreover, if one observes closely the revolution of night and day and the movement of the sun and the moon, one finds that for a long time they have been moving according to an extremely precise timetable. This timetable has never been disturbed, and their motion is continuous without even a slight pause. These matters deserve that a person reflect upon them and understand that for this universe there is one law, that a single Governor has established it, and that He is the true Creator and God, and the sole Manager of the universe.

Now, at the end of this lesson, the Noble Qur'an connects the laws and regulations which the Creator has put into operation in this universe, and according to which the Creator exercises His control over this universe, with the moral, legal and religious regulations which are being enacted for the voluntary sphere of human life. These regulations are a trial for you, just as your natural life has an end, so too your moral life has an end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verses 34–35:

"Wa ma ja'alna... ...wa ilayna turja'un" (And We did not grant immortality to any human before you... and to Us you will be returned.)

"Kullu nafsin dha'iqatul-mawt" (12:53) ("Every soul shall taste death.") This law of nature applies to life on this earth, and there is no exception to this rule. Therefore, all the living, and all the wise among the living, should keep this reality in mind.

Death is the end of every living thing. Human life on earth is a brief journey. All will return to Allah. The circumstances that a person encounters during this journey are a trial for him, a test.

"Wa nabluukum bish-sharri wal-khayri fitnah" (21:35) ("And We test you with evil and with good as a trial.") Being tested through evil is easy to understand: it becomes known how much a person endures patiently, how much he relies upon Allah, and how much he believes in the mercy of God. But how is there a test in goodness and well-being? This requires explanation.

The truth is that the test in goodness and well-being is more severe, although people consider it inferior to the test of evil. Most people can confront the test of adversity, but they cannot confront the test of prosperity. In sickness and weakness, people struggle against adversity, but in health and well-being, few people can withstand the test. They possess blind power over authority, or blind physical power, and in its use they fail. There will be countless people who bear poverty and hunger, and whose souls never urge them to disgrace or to seek unlawful provision by base means; but few are those who pass the test of wealth: who fulfil the right of wealth, do not become arrogant or proud, and abstain from luxury and indulgence.

There will be many who endure oppression and do not care for threats and intimidation, but few who can resist the allure of desires, rank and possessions in times of peace and security.

Many will be found who endure beatings, physical torment and wounds, but few who can remain patient in luxury, or stand upright against greed and avarice, because the love of the world bows the necks of the great, and people become so lax that their resolve breaks and they accept humiliation spiritually.

Through oppression and physical torture, a person's selfhood is awakened; endurance is produced in his nerves, and all the forces of the body rally to bear oppression. But ah, prosperity! It is a very dangerous trial. Through it the nerves become slack, a drowsiness overtakes the body's power of resistance, and the capacity for alertness and struggle is lost. We have made many such observations: a worker who was very successful in oppression and physical torture and kept standing firm, but when prosperity came, he failed the test of prosperity and abundance.

This is the story of man. Except for those whom Allah protects, and concerning whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer, for all his affairs are good. This privilege is granted only to the believer: if prosperity reaches him, he gives thanks to Allah, and that is good for him; and if hardship befalls him, he is patient, and that too is good for him." But such people are very few.

Therefore, a person in general, and a worker of the Islamic movement in particular, should be more vigilant in good times than in bad times. However, in both conditions, a true connection with the Lord, the Exalted, is the real guarantee of success.

Lesson No. 141 — At a Glance

In the previous lesson we travelled far across this universe. We studied the laws of nature in this creation and saw the end of humanity in the light of historical events. In this lesson the discourse turns back to the theme that we studied at the beginning of the surah: that the polytheists received the Messenger ﷺ and the revelation that came to him with mockery, and kept insisting upon shirk.

After this, the lesson mentions the hastiness and impatience of human nature, to the extent that these people even hurry the coming of the punishment of Allah. They are warned about this conduct and it is said that the outcome of mocking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will not be good. They are warned about this conduct and it is said that the outcome of mocking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will not be good. In this lesson they are also shown a scene of the shrinking of the shade of power of those who are influential, dominant and seize authority here, and a scene of the punishment of the Hereafter is also shown to them.

The lesson concludes on the theme that on the Day of Judgment the criminals will be held to a severe reckoning. Thus at the end, the themes of the reckoning of the Hereafter, the laws of nature, the nature of man, the Sunnah of Allah regarding human life, and the Sunnah of Allah regarding the callers to Islam are brought together.

﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you only for mockery: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" Yet they are disbelievers in the Most Merciful.﴾ (21:36)

These disbelievers themselves deny the very existence of the Most Merciful, although He is the Creator and Manager of this universe. And they do not like the reasonable commentary that is made by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on their deities and idols. Yet when they themselves deny the Most Merciful, they see no harm in it, although they are His servants, and then they deny the teachings of the Qur'an. This means that a great corruption has arisen in their nature, and they take by a measure different from the one by which they give, and they decide the truths wrongly.

Man has been created hasty by nature. Haste is placed in his temperament and in his very make-up. He always keeps his eyes fixed on what will emerge from behind the curtain of the future. He wants to take the secrets of the future into his own hands. He wants all his impressions to take the form of reality. He wants the promises made to him to come before him, even if they bring him pain. This situation changes when a person's connection with Allah is established. In that case, stability comes into his life. He becomes content, entrusts his affairs to Allah, and then does not act hastily. Faith is the name of certainty, patience, and tranquility.

These mushrikeen (polytheists), who demand the arrival of the punishment and say, "Why does it not come quickly?", also ask when the Last Day will come, that is, when the punishment of the Hereafter will occur, and when the punishment of this world will come, with which you threaten us. On this occasion, only a scene of the punishment of the Hereafter is presented before them, and they are warned that many people before you also mocked in this manner, but when the punishment came, they became a lesson for others.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 21, verses 42–43:

Qul man yakla'ukum... wa lahum minna yusahabun (21:42–43) (note: the Urdu reference reads 24:34)

Allah is the One who protects every living being, by night and by day, from various harms. This attribute is Ar-Rahman, that is, the Most Merciful. There is no other being besides Allah who can protect or help. O Messenger, ask them: is there anyone else besides Allah who is your protector and guardian? This question is in fact asked for the purpose of rebuke and reproach, and the interrogation is a negative one, meaning that there is no one. You are sunk in very great heedlessness. It is Allah alone who protects you by night and by day, and there is no other protector or guardian besides Him.

Bal hum... mu'ridun (21:42–43): "Rather, they turn away from the admonition of their Lord." The same question is put to them in another form.

Am lahum... min dununa (21:42–43): "Do they have gods who can support them against Us?" So that these gods might support and protect them in other matters. Never! This is the condition of the gods they have.

La yastati'una nasra anfusahum (21:42–43): "They cannot even help themselves." When they cannot even help themselves, how will they help others?

Wa la hum minna yusahabun (21:42–43): "Nor do they have any companionship from Us, nor any support, so that they might gain strength from a Powerful One, as Harun and Musa, peace be upon them, received support from Allah when Allah said: Go to Pharaoh."

Inni ma'akuma asma'u wa ara (20:46): "I am with you both, I hear and I see." These gods do not possess any power of their own. Nor do they receive the support of Allah, and therefore they cannot help anyone.

After pointing out this weakness in the beliefs of the polytheists, and after mocking them, and after seeing that their argument is devoid of proof, the context concludes the debate with them and turns to the question of why they are so entangled in this manner. After this, they are made to realize: reflect a little, and see how the Hand of Power is reducing the influence of these great men and pulling the ground from beneath their feet. Their sphere of influence is narrowing, although they were influential over a wide territory. They had strength and great authority.

Translation:

In fact, We had made them and their forefathers prosperous through inheritance; wealth had corrupted their nature. Their minds had become deranged, and their feelings and inclinations had changed. Their bond with God had weakened, and they did not reflect upon the many proofs in this universe that point to the Being of God. This was their trial, but it was a trial conducted through prosperity, and when Allah tests someone through prosperity, His test is severe, whereas in wealth the remembrance of God and the bond with Allah are needed all the more.

Thus the Quran seeks to awaken the feelings of these people by presenting them with another scene. This scene too is constantly found on this earth in the form of real events: a great kingdom breaks into pieces and shrinks; a mighty state becomes a collection of small principalities. After being a great power and dominant over the world, these become defeated states. A very great state becomes a small state; a large number becomes a small number, and instead of a wealthy kingdom it becomes a poor nation.

The manner of the speech is such that the hand of divine power shrinks these great kingdoms. When imagination does its work, a most blood-stirring scene appears before us. The slow movement of the ebb and flow of nations produces extremely frightening consequences.

"Afahum al-ghalibun" (21:44): "Will it be they who are the victors?" Will they not have the same happen to them as is happening to other nations, day and night? After this frightening scene of the ebb and flow of nations, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told to give them one last warning and admonition.

﴿Say, "I only warn you by revelation... but the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned."﴾ (54)

"People, consider: could it be that you are deaf? Why do you not listen? Otherwise the earth will slide from beneath your feet, and the hand of power will seize you and crush you. They are being warned against the arrogance of wealth and the intoxication of affluence."

The flow of the discourse (siyaq al-kalam) further sharpens its effect and, at the time of punishment, shows them their own state as a picture.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 46:

"And if a breath of your Lord's punishment touched them, they would surely say, 'Woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers.'" The word nafhah is applied in the sense of both goodness and mercy, meaning a breeze or a puff. Here it means a light breath of the punishment of Allah. That is, even if a slight breath of Allah's punishment touches them, they will confess their sins, but at that time confession will be of no benefit. Earlier in this surah, the cry of the people of the towns has already passed by, that when punishment came upon them, they made their confession.

"They cried, 'Woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers.' And they continued this cry until We made them like a harvested field, extinguished, with not a spark of life left among them" (21:14-15). But this confession came after the time had passed. Therefore, it is better for them to accept this warning before its time, before a breath of Allah's punishment comes upon them.

This lesson concludes with a final scene of the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection.

Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation), on Surah 21, verse 47:

ونضع الموازين... حسبين (74)

By "mithqal habbat min khardal" (a grain of mustard seed) is meant the smallest thing, one that weighs very little on the scale. On the Day of Reckoning, even this will not be overlooked, and the scale will be so sensitive that it will tip up or down by the weight of a mustard seed.

Therefore every soul should save as much as it can for tomorrow. Hearts should listen attentively to the one who warns. The heedless, those who turn away, and those who mock should take heed before a gust of the punishment of this world strikes them, or a whip of the punishment of the Hereafter is fixed upon their backs. Even if they escape the punishment of this world, the punishment of the Hereafter is ready for them, and in its scale there will be no injustice, not even to the weight of a mustard seed.

In this way, the extremely sensitive scale of the Hereafter has been harmonized with the extremely sensitive laws of nature of this universe. Likewise, the circumstances of the call and the nature of human beings have been interconnected, and all these matters have been declared to be the workings of the Hand of Divine Power. Through them, the unity of the single Administrator who works behind this universe is established, and this is the proof for the doctrine of Tawhid (the Oneness of God).

Lesson No. 241: At a Glance

This third lesson of the surah is a brief survey of the whole company of Messengers. It does not cover all the Messengers, but it mentions the great ones. Some are referred to only in a very brief allusion, some are described in some detail, and some are mentioned briefly.

Across all these allusions and both the detailed and brief accounts, one sees how much mercy Allah bestowed upon His Messengers, and what the end was of those who denied them despite seeing their clear signs and miracles. Moreover, there are accounts of the trials of the Messengers: sometimes they were tested through ease and sometimes through hardship, and how they succeeded in these tests.

It also shows that Allah always sent Messengers from among human beings, and that their creed was one and the same. Along with the creed, their method in discharging the duty of prophethood was also one. Despite differences of time and place, they appear as one single community and one single group.

That the Messengers had one doctrine and one community is evidence that Allah is One. Therefore the creed brought by the Messengers is one creed, the Giver of it is one, the Creator of the laws of nature in this universe is one, and this lesson also shows that all these Messengers, humanity and the universe are linked in one direction to one God: "Inna rabbukum fa'buduun" (Indeed, your Lord is I, so worship Me).

Lesson No. 241: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 48 to 29

*Wa laqad atainaa Musa...* up to *a-fa-antum lahu munkiroon* (21:48–50, in the Urdu rendering of this section)

In this surah it was mentioned that the polytheists mocked the Prophet (ﷺ), saying that he claimed to be a Messenger although he was a human being like them. Instead of accepting the Qur'an as revelation, they would say that it is sorcery, or poetry, or fabrication. This whole lesson therefore answers their accusation: Messengers were sent before him too, and it is the established practice of Allah that all Messengers were human beings, and sending a Book is no novelty either. Books were given to Messengers before as well. Moses and Aaron (peace be upon them) were given a Book.

The Book given to Moses (peace be upon him) was also a *Furqan*. *Furqan* is also an attribute of the Qur'an. Thus the chain of Messengers is one, their Books are one, and their attributes are one, because all the Books sent down by Allah were distinguishing between truth and falsehood, which is why they were called *Furqan*. They distinguished between guidance and misguidance. They distinguished between the Islamic system of life and the jahili system. They distinguished between Islamic tendencies and non-Islamic tendencies. Therefore they were generally called *Furqan*, and the Torah and the Qur'an were explicitly described as *Furqan*.

The Torah is also called here a *light* (*Nur*), because it illuminated the darknesses of ideas and concepts, and dispelled the darkness of falsehood. These are the kinds of darkness in which reason and understanding grope about, and the sun does not rise in the inner world of a human being until the flame of faith is kindled within him, he illuminates his environment, gives life a method, and determines the direction of life's undertakings, so that there is no discord between values, plans and aims.

Like the Qur'an, the Torah was also a *Dhikr* and a *Guidance* for the *muttaqeen* (the God-fearing). Through the Torah, the mention of Moses and the Children of Israel continues to this day. Yet what was the historical standing of the Children of Israel before the Torah? First, they were slaves of Pharaoh, who would slaughter their sons and let their daughters live, and who kept them in humiliation and under oppression. Here, the *muttaqeen* are further described as those who believe in the unseen and fear their Lord.

Those who fear their Lord unseen ﴿الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ (21:49), and who are apprehensive of the Hour ﴿وَهُم مِّنَ السَّاعَةِ مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ (21:49).

This is because those who fear Allah, though they have never seen Him, and who are apprehensive of the Hour and prepare for it and act accordingly, are the ones who benefit from this light and adopt the path of guidance. For such people the Book becomes a reminder. It keeps reminding them to turn back to Allah. Through it, they are mentioned among people, so that it becomes, as it were, their identity.

This was the status of Musa and Harun: ﴿وَهَٰذَا ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ﴾ (21:50), "And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down." This is not something new or strange. It is an event that has occurred before. It is the known and established sunnah (the way or practice) of Allah.

﴿أَفَأَنتُمْ لَهُ مُنكِرُونَ﴾ (21:50), "Will you then deny it?" Why does this seem unusual to you? Did not Allah's messengers come before this?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 52:

"When he said to his father and his people, 'What are these images to which you are devoted?' (21:52)"

Their very statement is itself evidence of their guidance and right direction. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) used a very accurate word for those stones, wood and other materials, namely "timāthīl" (images, statues). He did not call them "ilah" (deities), and he sharply challenged them on the fact that you people worship them with great attachment. The meaning of "'ākifūn" (devoted, remaining in attendance) shows that these people remained constantly bowed before them, although they may have also been engaged in other affairs; but their hearts were with these idols. Therefore, it is as though they were continuously bowed before them, in a figurative sense. For this reason the expression was framed in these words: "you remain bowed before them day and night."

Their answer and only proof was this:

﴿They said: "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ [21:53]

This response shows that when a people blindly follows the customs of their forefathers, their power of thought and reason becomes frozen. Faith, however, teaches a person freedom, breadth of thinking and vision, and a genuine assessment of every matter and every situation. It commands him to reflect on every claim and weigh it on its true merits. Therefore, firm faith in Allah has this aspect as well, which is very important: through the doctrine of Tawhid and the rejection of shirk, a person is freed from superstitions, blind imitation, and those same notions and beliefs. Hereditary customs that have neither any basis in reason nor any proof behind them are easily abandoned.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 54:

Qala laqad... fi dalal mubin (45) — [the Qur'anic text here is cited as: "He said: Indeed you and your fathers have been in clear error."]

The mere fact that idol-worship was practised by one's forefathers does not change the true reality and worth of these idols, nor can it grant them a sanctity that they do not actually possess. For values do not come into existence merely through the practice of forefathers; rather, they are formed on the basis of truth and utility, and their status is determined through independent thinking.

When Hazrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) spoke these words with great fearlessness, made a realistic assessment, and spoke plainly, there was an earthquake in the world of their beliefs, and they began to ask [questions].

They said: "Have you come to us with the truth, or are you one of those who jest?" (21:55)

This question appears to come from someone who is not fully confident in his own beliefs and actions, for he has never reflected on or investigated what he believes and what he does. He does these things merely out of illusion, imitation, and without thought. He does not know what the truth is, although beliefs and acts of worship are matters that must rest upon sound proofs. Individuals and peoples who lack a clear and pure conception of the belief in Tawhid fall prey to such illusions, and their thoughts too are neither pure nor clear.

Consider how Hazrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) speaks with such confidence and certainty. He possesses correct knowledge of his Lord, and he speaks with the firmness of a believer.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verse 56:

He said: "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, and I am a witness to that." (21:56)

Allah is the one Lord. He alone is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and He is Lord because He is their Creator; that is, He is the one God by two attributes, and these two cannot be separated. The first is that He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who sustains and governs them. The second is that He also brought them into being. This is the correct belief. The belief of the polytheists of Arabia, however, was quite reasonable in their own way: they regarded their idols as lords but did not regard them as creators. They acknowledged that Allah alone is the Creator, yet, knowing that the other gods had created nothing, they still worshipped them.

Abraham (peace be upon him) bears witness like a witness about whom there is no doubt.

"And I am of those who bear witness to that" (21:56, as rendered in the Urdu text: "وانا علی ذلکم من الشھدین", 12:65 in the source's reference). "I bear witness to it before you." At the time of the creation of the heavens and the earth, Abraham was not present, nor was he an eyewitness to the creation of himself or of his people. Yet the matter is so clear and so established that a believer can testify to it as an eyewitness would. The truth is that every thing in this universe bears testimony to the unity of the Creator. All the perfections of the human personality, physical and mental, are together an eloquent proof that the Creator is one and that He alone is the Governor. Likewise, the law of nature that runs this entire universe, including man, is also one, and it operates and directs as He wills.

The one from Abraham's people who was conducting this conversation with him was told by Abraham that he had made a decision regarding their idols, and that it would certainly be carried out.

﴿And by Allah, I will surely plot against your idols ... after you have turned your backs and gone away.﴾ (75)

They left unstated what decision they made regarding these idols. They did not mention it. The context of the discourse also does not clarify how they answered him. Perhaps they were content that he could not cause any harm to our idols, and so they disregarded it.

Then he made them into fragments, except for the largest of them, that they might turn to it (85). What happened? All the idols were smashed to pieces. They were reduced to heaps of small stones, and the wooden ones remained as broken pieces of wood. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) left the largest idol intact.

"So that they might turn to it" (21:58): "perhaps they will turn to him (ﷺ)..." And they would ask him how this incident occurred and why he did not rise to defend the smaller idols. Perhaps in this way they would be ready to reconsider the whole matter afresh and come onto the right path. They would come to know that worshipping idols is a futile matter.

When the people came, they saw that their idols lay smashed to pieces on the ground. Only the big idol stood upright like an idol, but they did not ask it anything. Nor did they themselves reflect: if these were gods, how did such treatment befall them, and if this one standing there is the great god, why did it not defend those smaller gods? They did not let this question arise in their minds; indeed it did not arise, because when superstitions settle into the intellect, the intellect becomes inactive and abandons its true function. When people begin blind imitation, their minds too are locked, and they do not engage in contemplation, reflection and deliberation on any matter.

"They said, [...] surely he is one of the wrongdoers" (95). Now they recalled that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had also argued with his father about these idols. Besides his father, he had also said to other people, "Why do you worship these images?" And then they reported that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had also issued the threat that when the people had gone away, he would deal with them.

They said: "We heard a young man mention them, who is called Ibrahim."

This indicates that at that time Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was a young man. Allah had guided him while he was still young. Therefore, regarding the worship of these idols as a repugnant act, he resolved to break their idols.

The question is: at that time, had he been given the command through prophethood and revelation, or not? Or was it inspired to him before his prophethood? On the basis of that inspiration, he had begun to invite his father and other people to the truth. This is the more prevalent view. However, it is also possible that they used the word "fata" (a young man) for him for this reason: firstly, to belittle him; and secondly, because they did not have much information about him.

"Yuqal lahu Ibrahim" (12:06): "the one called Ibrahim." This diminutive and passive form they were using because this is not an important man, nor is there any danger from him. But in our view, the first opinion is the more preferable, that Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was a young man.

Note: The source text as given begins with "قالوآ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ یابرھیم", where the quoted verse is abbreviated with ellipsis, so I have not supplied the omitted words. Translating the passage exactly as it stands:

"They said, '...O Ibrahim.' (26) It is a surprising matter that their idols were smashed to pieces, yet they still insisted that these were our gods. When Ibrahim was mocking them, he was alone and they were very many. But he looked at matters with an open heart and mind. Therefore, he could only mock these senseless people, and so he gave them an answer that was fitting for people like them."

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said in this answer: "Nay, this great one of theirs did it; so ask them, if they can speak." (Qur'an 21:63)

There was a veiled jest in the response of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). About this serious jest of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) it cannot be said that he spoke a falsehood. The lengthy discussion that the exegetes (mufassirin) have undertaken regarding the causes and interpretations of this phrase is not necessary. This matter is very simple. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) wished to tell the people: are these idols so lacking in knowledge that they cannot even tell who broke them? Did I break them, or did this big idol break them? The one who cannot even move. For these are mere inanimate objects (jamadat), and they have no power of perception at all. Even though you are human beings, you are such that your faculties of perception have become frozen. You cannot distinguish between a matter that is possible and permissible to occur and a matter that is impossible to occur. You are conducting this inquiry only because you think I broke them or this big idol did; then ask them, if they are able to speak. It appears that this strange jest shook them for a moment; they began to think and to reflect.

Fa-rajaʿū... innakum antumu al-ẓālimūn (46)

This was the beginning of a good way of thinking within them. They realised that there was a fundamental weakness in their position. Those who worship idols and images, this in reality is wrong-doing (ẓulm). For the first time it seems that their eyes were opened and they began to think that the path on which they were walking without thought was very wrong.

But this was only a flash of light in the world of their thought and understanding. Darkness, as before, prevailed again. A kind of throbbing arose in their dead hearts, but soon they fell silent again and became stuck in stagnation.

Then they were turned back upon their heads [...] they cannot speak. (56)

In the first phrase, they had indeed returned to their hearts and minds, and in the second phrase, which says that they turned back upside down, abandoning their heads, it is as though they turned back on their heels. They also gave up using their heads for thought. The first movement was towards their conscience, that they should reflect and plan, and the second movement was a reversal; having abandoned reflection and contemplation, they turned back again. The senseless words that came out of their mouths were themselves the proof against them. Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) argument was precisely this: see, these idols cannot even speak.

When matters reached this point, even a person of Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) forbearing nature becomes somewhat angry with them, because their lack of understanding is so evident that it is difficult for a person to remain patient about it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 21, verses 66–67:

Qala afata'buduna... afala ta'qilun (21:66–67)

Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) words reveal his feelings of distress. He appears somewhat angry, and he is greatly astonished that these people are engaged in such worthless and unreasonable thought and conduct.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-Anbiya', verses 68–69:

They said: [Burn him] and [...] (86) "...".

What a mighty god they have, whose helpers are their worshippers! These helpless ones do not even have control over their own benefit and harm; they cannot help themselves, nor can they help their devotees. They issued the order: "Burn him!" But from the other side too an order was issued. It was the command of the true, absolute Sovereign, and He nullified the first order.

﴿We said: "O fire, be cool and a means of safety for Ibrahim."﴾ (96)

So the fire that they had kindled became cool for Ibrahim and became a cause of safety for him. How? This question arises only about the fire of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)? By the words "Kun" (Be!) and "Kawni" (it is), this universe came into existence, and great worlds came into being.

﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it "Be," and it is.﴾ (36:82) So we do not even raise the question of how the fire failed to burn him, although the well-known, familiar and observed way is that fire burns living bodies. When the Divine Being said to the fire "Burn," it began to burn. That same Being said to it "Do not burn, and become cold," and it became cool and a means of safety. The only difference between the two commands is that we are accustomed to one result and not accustomed to the other.

Those who compare the acts of God with human acts are the ones before whom this question arises: how did this happen, and how was it possible? But those who understand the difference between God and human beings do not have this question arise in their minds. They do not seek the causes of such events, whether the cause is scientific or non-scientific, because this matter concerns the command of God, not causes and means, especially not the search for cause and effect according to human measures. Those who interpret the Qur'an's accounts of miracles according to scientific measures, that is, cause and effect, take the wrong path. The correct interpretation of miracles is to entrust them to the command of God, because the acts of God cannot be measured by the measures by which we measure human matters.

It is both our duty and what we should do to believe in these events, because God is the Creator and Fashioner, and a fashioner can make his creations in whatever way he wills. How it happened that the fire became cold and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) remained safe and sound within it: the Qur'an has given no explanation or rationale for this, because with our human faculties of perception we cannot comprehend this thing. Therefore, apart from the text of the Qur'an, we have no other proof, and we should not demand one.

The cooling of the fire upon Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is an example of things that happen in this world too, but we do not take notice of them, whereas history took notice of this important event. In human history, individuals and communities have suffered even greater oppressions, such terrible and frightful persecutions that no one can even imagine surviving them and coming out unharmed, yet people still emerge. Great blazing fires of oppression and violence are lit and people are thrown into them, yet they survive and escape, and this fire of oppression and violence grows cold. Outwardly this fire seems a great evil, but for those oppressed it becomes a great good.

This is a miracle: "O fire, be cool and a means of safety for Ibrahim." It is repeated again and again in the lives of individuals, communities and nations; especially from the standpoint of ideas, beliefs and movements, when the command of God comes, human words become null. All plots come to an end, because the command of God is the supreme command.
